requiredFindings.problem: The suffix edit also removes the common Objects rule without replacement. This loses the explicit distinction between canonical writer key order and order-independent reader admission, together with the common exact-key rule for composite values. Item 13a still forbids duplicate keys and closes the header, but it refers nested field admission to item 13c; its remaining text does not explicitly retain reader acceptance of any object-key order. The wire-spelling column fixes canonical forms, so deleting that distinction leaves whether a semantically identical key permutation must be accepted unspecified. This is a separate contract change outside the r5 response table and contradicts its claim that nothing else of substance changed.

evidence.note: r4 explicitly says: Objects have exactly the listed keys, written in the listed order. Readers accept any order, but no extra, missing or duplicate key. The r4-to-r5 diff deletes this entire line.
The revised common rules go directly from string/whole-value/suffix rules to the header. There is no replacement Objects rule or explicit reader acceptance of any key order.

Parsing rejects duplicate keys at every level and header validation requires an exact schema. For field values the reader delegates to the complete item 13c predicate; this does not replace the deleted writer-versus-reader order rule.
K7 is spelled {bytes:<u64>,truncated:<bool>}. The reader-order exception no longer states that the reversed-key spelling is admissible.

The exact pinned subjects confirm the deletion. {"bytes":1,"truncated":false} and {"truncated":false,"bytes":1} parse to the same JSON object; each is 29 bytes, below K7 V=48. r4 explicitly accepts either order. r5 no longer explicitly requires that behavior. This is textual evidence, not a product-reader failure.
The response table maps the five r4 items and states Nothing else of substance changed from r4; it does not map the object-rule deletion.

requiredFindings.fix: Restore the r4 Objects common rule (or an equivalent operative rule): writers use the listed key order, readers accept any order, and composite objects have exactly the keys permitted by their selected listed form, with no extra, missing or duplicate keys. Keep item 13a's whole-line duplicate/header checks. Add a C-4 reader positive with a permuted composite key order that canonicalizes on re-encoding, and nested extra/missing-key negatives, while retaining the canonical byte-identical writer round trips. This does not require any change to the r5 prescope partition, marker protocol, or lawful path suffixes.
